oneLiner: A retailer, ad network and the largest cloud in one P&L, where the market is betting that AWS's sold-out AI capacity turns a capex budget heading well above $220B into a durable step-up in operating income. Reported EPS is not the test - Anthropic marks have swung it for a year - so the stock works only if operating income compounds faster than the cash goes out.
thesis: AWS is accelerating into a booked pipeline. Growth stepped up again in Q3 2026 and management now projects AWS above 40% in both 2027 and 2028, backed by a backlog that more than doubled in a year - capex is being spent against contracted work, not hope.

Operating leverage is visible through the spend. Operating margin rose from ~10% to a record 13.9% over four quarters while quarterly capex roughly doubled; AWS earns ~63% of operating income on ~23% of revenue, so mix alone lifts the consolidated margin.

Custom silicon is a second franchise. Amazon has disclosed $225B+ of future Trainium revenue commitments including Anthropic and OpenAI (24/7 Wall St, Oct 2026), and inference is now well over half of AWS AI revenue; every Trainium rack that replaces a merchant GPU keeps gross margin inside AWS.
Retail now funds itself. North America's operating margin is near 8% even in a quarter without Prime Day, so the non-AWS business adds to returns rather than diluting them.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30, 2026; reported Oct 29, 2026)
points: Net sales $201.9B, +12% YoY (+13% ex-FX), at the top of the $197-202B guide; Amazon says the Prime Day shift into Q2 cost ~400bp of growth.
AWS $46.0B, +39% YoY (fastest in nearly five years), operating income $17.8B (38.7% margin); backlog $578B; annualized run rate $184B.
Operating income $28.1B, +61% YoY, above the $22.5-26.5B guide; record 13.9% operating margin.
Diluted EPS $1.89 (net income $20.7B) vs $1.95 a year ago, which included a $9.5B pre-tax Anthropic gain; below ~$1.96-1.97 consensus.
Advertising $19.6B (+11-12%), first miss in seven quarters on Prime Day timing; North America $112.9B (+6%, op income $8.7B); International $43.1B (+5%, op income $1.6B); TTM FCF -$42.4B.

segments: North America ~56% of Q3 2026 revenue ($112.9B, +6%, 7.7% operating margin).
AWS ~23% of revenue ($46.0B) but ~63% of operating income ($17.8B of $28.1B).
Advertising ($19.6B in Q3) is reported inside the geographic segments - the profit mix-shifter; Q4 guided to high-teens growth.

Strategic stakes: Anthropic ($8B invested through 2025, plus $5B in April 2026 with up to $20B more on milestones), marked up after Anthropic's May 2026 Series H at a reported ~$965B post-money; carrying value ~$190B at Jun 30 per press reports (unverified).
competitive: Cloud: Azure and Google Cloud grew faster through 2025; AWS's reacceleration to 39% has closed the growth gap on a much larger base.
AI silicon: Trainium vs Nvidia GPUs and Google TPUs; Anthropic co-designs with Annapurna Labs, OpenAI is a second anchor.
Retail: Walmart's e-commerce and Temu/Shein at the low end; fulfillment density keeps Amazon's cost lead.
Advertising: #3 behind Google and Meta; the Q3 miss shows it is more tied to retail events than the software-like margins suggest.
Satellite: Amazon Leo enters a market Starlink dominates by thousands of satellites.
moat: Prime plus the densest fulfillment network in Western retail is a two-sided lock-in no rival has replicated. AWS adds switching costs, a $578B contracted backlog and proprietary silicon (Trainium, Graviton), while advertising monetizes first-party purchase intent that Google and Meta cannot see.
risks: Capex outruns cash. Trailing free cash flow fell to -$42.4B through Q3 2026 and 2027 capex is guided 'meaningfully more' than 2026's ~$220B, so FCF stays negative into a third year and the return on the buildout is taken on trust until AWS growth converts.

Earnings quality. Trailing net income is still ~129% of operating income because of the 2026 Anthropic gains ($16.8B Q1, $53.4B Q2); Q3 had no comparable mark, so trailing EPS and P/E flatter the operating business and will fall as those quarters roll off.

Circular demand. Amazon funds Anthropic and OpenAI, both commit large sums to AWS and Trainium, and the stake marks lift EPS - if either lab's growth or funding stalls, backlog, AWS growth and non-operating income fall together.
Input-cost inflation. Part of the 2026 capex raise was memory prices, not capacity - the same dollars buy less compute, compressing infrastructure ROI and lifting 2027-28 depreciation.

Revenue growth is decelerating at the top line. Consolidated growth slowed to +12% in Q3 from +20% in Q2; Prime Day timing explains ~400bp, but retail at +5-6% and advertising at ~11% mean the consolidated story now rests on AWS alone.
catalysts: Early Dec 2026: AWS re:Invent - Trainium3 ramp and Trainium4 roadmap, Anthropic capacity deliveries (debate 1).
~Early Feb 2027: Q4 2026 report - sales vs $240-247B and operating income vs $28.5-33.5B guide, advertising back to high-teens, the formal 2027 capex figure (debates 2, 3).
Anthropic IPO timing (confidential draft filed Jun 2026; listing date unverified) - turns the stake mark into a market price (debate 3).
~Late Apr 2027: Q1 2027 report - first quarter tested against the 40%+ AWS growth projection (debate 1).

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: FCF is distorted by ~$220B of 2026 capex and more in 2027, and trailing GAAP earnings carry Anthropic marks - forward operating EPS is the cleanest anchor available.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Oct 29) was an operating beat and a headline miss. Net sales were $201.9B (+12%, +13% ex-FX), at the top of the guide, with Amazon attributing ~400bp of lost growth to Prime Day moving into Q2. Operating income rose 61% to $28.1B, $1.6B above the top of the guide, for a record 13.9% margin. AWS did the work: $46.0B (+39%, fastest in nearly five years) at a 38.7% margin, a $578B backlog more than double a year earlier, and inference now well over half of AWS AI revenue. Advertising missed for the first time in seven quarters at $19.6B (~11-12%), and diluted EPS of $1.89 trailed consensus because net income ($20.7B) sat below operating income: there was no Anthropic mark this quarter (exact other-income line unverified), against a $9.5B pre-tax gain a year ago. Purchases of property and equipment were reportedly $77.3B in the quarter (single-sourced), and trailing free cash flow fell to -$42.4B while trailing operating cash flow rose 29% to $168.3B.
guidanceProse: Q4 2026 guide: net sales $240-247B (+12-16%) against ~$244.5B consensus, and operating income $28.5-33.5B vs $25.0B in Q4 2025; the $31.0B midpoint sits ~$2B below the ~$33B Street figure. Advertising is guided back to high-teens growth. Full-year 2026 cash capex stays ~$220B, and Jassy said 2027 capex will be 'meaningfully more' with no figure until the Q4 call; the shares fell ~7% after hours on that line. The offset is the strongest AWS outlook Amazon has given: revenue growth projected above 40% in both 2027 and 2028.

verdict.stance: Positive - on operating EPS, not the marks
verdict.summary: Q3 settled the demand question in the bull direction - AWS accelerated and management put a 40%+ number on 2027-28 - and turned the debate to cash: 2027 capex goes up again and free cash flow stays negative longer. Valued on 2027 operating EPS of about $10.40, the bull case (AWS above 40% with margin) is worth ~38% more than the base and the bear case (capex keeps rising while AWS slows) ~35% less; the skew improved slightly with the higher bull probability. Two things would change the view: a formal 2027 capex figure far above AWS revenue growth (capex up 40%+ with AWS below 35%), or AWS growth falling below 30% in any 2027 quarter.
wtb: AWS grows at least 35% YoY in every quarter through Q4 2027, in line with the 40%+ projection - capacity, not demand, sets the pace.
2027 operating margin reaches at least ~14.5% (vs ~13.3% implied for 2026) despite the depreciation from the 2026-27 buildout.
Trailing free cash flow bottoms by mid-2027 and operating cash flow keeps growing 25%+ a year, so 2028 FCF can turn positive.
The market pays ~27x 2027 operating EPS at end-2027 and gives the Anthropic stake no extra credit.

bear.why: AI capacity is digested: AWS slows to the high-20s as anchor labs pause, retail and ads stay soft and 2027 revenue grows ~11% on ~$828B. Depreciation from the buildout holds net margin at ~10%. With capex up again and FCF negative, the market pays a retail-like multiple.

base.why: AWS grows ~35-40% as booked capacity comes online, ads high-teens, retail mid-single digits: revenue +15%. Operating margin ~14.5%, net margin ~12% after tax. FCF is still negative through most of 2027, which keeps the multiple slightly below Amazon's recent range.

bull.why: AWS clears 40% as Trainium and the $578B backlog convert; revenue +20% and AWS mix lifts net margin to ~13.5%. A visible 2028 FCF inflection and a second chip franchise earn a low-30s multiple.

scenarioModel.note: 2026 revenue assumes Q1 $181.5B + Q2 $200.6B + Q3 $201.9B + Q4 guide midpoint $243.5B = ~$828B; 2026 operating income on the same basis ~$110B (~13.3%). EPS = revenue x net margin / ~11.0B diluted shares (10.93B in Q3 2026, +0.8%/yr): bear 920 x 10.0% = $92.0B / 11.0 = $8.36; base 955 x 12.0% = $114.6B / 11.0 = $10.42; bull 990 x 13.5% = $133.7B / 11.0 = $12.15. EPS excludes non-operating investment marks (Anthropic and other stakes assumed zero). Multiples apply to FY2027 EPS at end-2027. Probability-weighted value ~$289. Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.bull: Q3 accelerated without help, the backlog more than doubled in a year, $225B+ of Trainium commitments are signed, and management now projects 40%+ for 2027 and 2028; the constraint is power and chips, not customers.
debates.bear: Two anchor labs (Anthropic, OpenAI) drive much of the backlog; if either slows funding, bookings can be renegotiated and growth reverts toward the high-teens of 2024-25.
debates.view: Q3 passed our bullish 35% signpost, so we raised the bull probability. This still sets the multiple (22x vs 32x); the test now is whether 40% shows up in reported 2027 quarters, not in projections.

signpost.when: Q4 2026 report ~early Feb 2027, then Q1 2027 ~late Apr 2027

debates.q: Does the capex earn its return, and when does free cash flow turn?
debates.bull: Capex is spent against contracted demand; AWS margin near 39%, trailing operating cash flow up 29% and a record consolidated margin show the new capacity earns more than its depreciation.
debates.bear: Trailing FCF went from +$14.8B to -$42.4B in a year, Q3 capex reportedly ran ~$20B above estimates, and 2027 is guided higher again - the cash return keeps moving out a year.
debates.view: Acceptable while AWS margin holds and AWS growth keeps pace with capex; the bear case starts if the 2027 figure implies capex growth well ahead of AWS revenue growth. Watch the ratio, not the dollar figure.

signpost.metric: Formal 2027 capex outlook vs AWS revenue growth
signpost.threshold: bearish if 2027 capex guided up 40%+ (above ~$310B) with Q4 AWS growth below 35%

debates.q: How much of EPS is Anthropic, and does the stake deserve credit?
debates.bull: The marks are real value: the stake was set by a ~$965B third-party round, and an IPO would give it a market price Amazon could monetize.
debates.bear: Trailing net income is still ~129% of operating income; the marks are circular (Amazon funds the customer that buys AWS) and reverse if the valuation falls. Q3 showed the flip side: no mark, and EPS missed while operations beat.
debates.view: Q3 was the clean quarter we wanted - operating income beat the top of the guide without help from marks. We keep giving the stake no credit and value operating EPS only; expect trailing EPS to fall in Q2 2027 when the $53.4B gain rolls off.

signpost.metric: Q4 operating income vs guide; size of non-operating gains
signpost.threshold: operating income below the $31.0B guide midpoint while EPS beats on marks = red flag
